summary: With no matching root-to-leaf sum, a tree can force every node and leaf path to be examined. The iterative depth-first traversal visits each node once and stores height-proportional pending state.

optimality.argument: Choose a complete n-node tree and a target unequal to every root-to-leaf sum. Until every leaf path has been ruled out, an unexamined leaf could still complete a valid sum, so the worst case requires Omega(n) node inspection. The current DFS pushes and pops each node once while carrying its exact path sum, giving O(n) time and O(h) pending stack space.

replacement_checks.evidence: For an absent target, every leaf path must be ruled out; a complete tree contains Theta(n) nodes across those paths.
Each tree node is pushed once with one accumulated sum, popped once, and processed with constant work.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover a successful path, an absent sum, and an empty tree; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
